subject.title: [Bug] WebChat: optimistic USER messages are lost (not just hidden) when chat.send returns before the durable transcript lands — full-replace history reconcile drops them

question: Should WebChat `chat.send` guarantee a durable user-turn transcript entry immediately after ACK, or should ACK remain only an admission signal with UI-side pending-message preservation?
rationale: Current main documents non-blocking ACKs and relies on later recorder/runtime persistence, while the open candidate PR changes that durability boundary and prior review found merge-risk in the current branch direction.

options.title: Require durable post-ACK user turn
options.body: Adopt a gateway-side persistence contract and port it through the current shared recorder/session-accessor boundary with same-session, rollover, media, hook, and duplicate-suppression proof.

options.title: Keep ACK as admission only
options.body: Keep the current non-blocking contract, close or reject the candidate PR direction, and add visible failure/audit surfacing for runs that never reach transcript persistence.

recommendation.title: Require durable post-ACK user turn
recommendation.body: Adopt a gateway-side persistence contract and port it through the current shared recorder/session-accessor boundary with same-session, rollover, media, hook, and duplicate-suppression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice centers on the shared user-turn recorder and transcript persistence boundary that shakkernerd introduced.
